subject: Re: unexpected sub-second billing spikes — export request for raw traces
messages:
From: Priyanka Sethi <priyanka@wavescale.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected billing spike on Jun 19 export

Hi Neha,

We noticed a ~3x spike in our token invoice line for Jun 19 (UTC window 23:00-23:05). We haven't changed traffic patterns and our side shows steady request rates. Can you share any insight on what your metering counted as tokens during that short window?

Attached is our quick CSV export from our side showing request timestamps; the billing line item is on invoice INV-20260630.

Thanks — this is pushing our month-end close; can you put the invoice on hold while we sort?

—Priyanka
Priyanka Sethi
Head of Platform Ops, WaveScale
attachments: spike_sample_20260619.csv
From: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: david_kim@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 17:05:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected billing spike on Jun 19 export

Forwarding WaveScale's ticket — they report a short high-cost spike in our Jun 19 metering. Priyanka attached a CSV from their side (see original below).

Asking billing + account to triage:
- Could this be related to sub-second request batching or a duplicate ingestion on our collector?
- If we need to pull raw request traces (request-id level) for that 5-minute window, please advise what format WaveScale needs.

Ben — can you confirm if we should place INV-20260630 on hold pending the investigation? Marissa, FYI for finance implications.

Thanks,
Neha
Principal Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwoodinference.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected billing spike on Jun 19 export

Thanks Neha — looking at the telemetry now. Quick notes:

- Initial aggregation shows a cluster of ~1.2M tokens in 23:00:42–23:01:08 UTC which doesn't match the request counts from WaveScale's CSV.
- Root candidates: a) duplicate requests replayed from their edge (same request-id repeated within sub-second intervals), b) our streaming stitcher counted partial-tokens as separate micro-tokens for a short period due to a config flip on Jun 19 23:00:37 UTC, c) third-party proxy replays.

I can export request-level traces for that 5-minute window but we need to agree on a minimal set of fields for WaveScale: request_id, model, seq_len_prompt, seq_len_completion, token_count, server_received_ts, server_sent_ts. The traces are heavy; I'll produce a filtered CSV + a token id list.

Attaching a small sample of request ids we think are part of the anomaly: token_trace_ids.txt (redacted). If WaveScale wants full traces we'll need 24–48 hours to pull and scrub PII.

Also: we have a short-lived internal flag that changed batching thresholds at 23:00:37; I'm attaching the ops note and will check rollout logs. If the flag flip is the cause, we can propose a goodwill credit for the delta.

—David
David Kim
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: token_trace_ids.txt
From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Priyanka Sethi <priyanka@wavescale.com>, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike on Jun 19 export

Priyanka — thanks for flagging and Neha/David for quick triage.

We're happy to put INV-20260630 on hold for now. Please confirm you want the hold applied to the entire invoice or just the contested line item (token usage). If you'd like, we can also send a provisional credit pending the final audit.

Could you confirm whether you want the raw traces or the summarized CSV (request_id + token_count + timestamps)? Full traces require scrubbing and an NDA amendment for PII; summarized CSV is usually sufficient for metering reconciliation.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Priyanka Sethi <priyanka@wavescale.com>, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike on Jun 19 export — finance hold and next steps

Hi all,

Finance will place a hold on INV-20260630 (full invoice) until we receive the reconciliation CSV or final audit notes. Please note the hold will not delay collections beyond 30 days without mutual agreement; we can extend the hold if WaveScale provides a timeline for the audit.

Requested deliverables from Redwood OPS/Billing to WaveScale by EOD 23 Jul:
- Summarized reconciliation CSV: request_id, token_count_billed, token_count_wave, server_received_ts, server_sent_ts (CSV)
- A short explanation (1–2 paragraphs) of the root cause and whether internal flags affected token counting
- Any proposed pro-rata credit amount or correction entry to appear on the next invoice

We will route the final credit (if approved) through accounting and update the invoice reference. Ben — please track approval from WaveScale and HubSpot deal HS-4321.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference
